newsitem.title: GERMANY: NATO says will not hunt Bosnia war criminals.
newsitem.headline: NATO says will not hunt Bosnia war criminals.

text.p: A top NATO military officer said on Tuesday the alliance-led force in Bosnia would not start hunting down war criminals.
General Klaus Naumann, chairman of NATO's military committee told the Flensburger Tageblatt newspaper that countries contributing to the force would not back such a mandate.
NATO decided on Monday that an alliance-led Stabilisation Force of between 25,000 and 30,000 troops should stay in Bosnia next year to cement the country's fragile peace.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and others had called for a more rigorous pursuit of war criminals in the former Yugoslav republic.
"The necessary approval from all those supplying troops will not be forthcoming," Naumann told the newspaper.

He said that from a moral point of view the war criminals belong in front of the Hague Tribunal. But from a military point of view, hunting war criminals would raise risks of casualties among soldiers and civilians.
